discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: In 1998 Jaksch, Bruder, Cirac, Gardiner and Zoller showed that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Bloch and coworkers observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition, and this turned an idea into a working experimental platform. Cirac and Zoller also supplied the theoretical framework for engineering lattice Hamiltonians, gauge fields and entangling operations with light. Bloch's group then used this toolbox to study many-body physics directly: single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy, many-body localisation, and dynamics far from equilibrium. The resulting field of analogue quantum simulation now underpins neutral-atom quantum computing and has changed the design of optical lattice clocks, which use the same Hubbard physics to reach 10^-19 precision. The work is a clear example of theory and experiment advancing together to create a new way of solving problems that classical computers cannot handle.
